There was widespread neuronal loss with reactive gliosis throughout the grey matter (Supplementary Figure 3). The most striking pathological finding was the accumulation of foamy macrophages, predominantly in a perivascular distribution, throughout the white matter

records.label: Six individuals from four families with bi-allelic NRROS variants
records.onset: seizure onset within the first year of life
quotes: We report six individuals from four families with bi-allelic variants in NRROS. All affected individuals had neurodegenerative disease with refractory epilepsy, developmental regression, and reduced white matter volume with delayed myelination.

The clinical course in affected individuals began with normal development or mild developmental delay, and the onset of seizures occurred within the first year of life, followed by developmental regression. Intracranial calcification was detected in three individuals.

notes.statement: Dong et al. (2020) showed by confocal microscopy in HEK293T cells that wild-type and mutant NRROS proteins co-localized with latent TGF-beta-1 intracellularly, but by flow cytometry the mutant proteins failed to anchor latent TGF-beta-1 at the cell surface, unlike wild-type NRROS. Wild-type NRROS rescued the defect of the disease-associated mutants in presenting latent TGF-beta-1 to the cell surface.
quotes: Using confocal microscopy in HEK293T cells, we demonstrate that wild-type and mutant NRROS proteins co-localize with latent TGF-β1 intracellularly.

However, using flow cytometry, we show that our mutant NRROS proteins fail to anchor latent TGF-β1 at the cell surface in comparison to wild-type NRROS. Moreover, wild-type NRROS rescues the defect of our disease-associated mutants in presenting latent TGF-β1 to the cell surface.

notes.statement: Dong et al. (2020) found that the disease-causing NRROS variants involved two significant functional NRROS domains and resulted in aberrant proteins with impaired ability to anchor latent TGF-beta-1 on the cell surface; they suggested that loss of NRROS function causes a severe childhood-onset neurodegenerative condition with features suggestive of a disordered response to inflammation.
quotes: The disease-causing NRROS variants involve two significant functional NRROS domains. These variants result in aberrant NRROS proteins with impaired ability to anchor latent TGF-β1 on the cell surface.
our findings suggest that loss of NRROS function causes a severe childhood-onset neurodegenerative condition with features suggestive of a disordered response to inflammation.

notes.statement: Dong et al. (2020) noted that the phenotypic features in affected individuals were consistent with those observed in the Nrros knockout mouse and overlapped with those of the human condition associated with TGF-beta-1 deficiency.
quotes: The phenotypic features in affected individuals are consistent with those observed in the Nrros knockout mouse, and they overlap with those seen in the human condition associated with TGF-β1 deficiency.

notes.statement: Smith et al. (2020) found that foamy white matter macrophages in the brain of an affected patient were positive for CD68, MHC class II and p22phox but did not react with CD163, IBA1, NRROS, P2Y12 or TMEM119. Loss of P2Y12 staining and weak TMEM119 suggested marked parenchymal microglial abnormalities, and upregulated p22phox suggested that loss of NRROS might increase p22phox-NOX2 binding and superoxide formation.
quotes: These foamy cells immunoreacted with CD68, MHC Class II (CR3/43), and p22phox (Fig. 2c–f), but did not immunoreact with CD163, Iba1, NRROS, CD3, P2Y12, or TMEM119

p22phox was markedly up-regulated in PVMs in our case, suggesting that an absence of functional NRROS may result in increased p22phox-NOX2 binding, with the potential for increased superoxide radical formation.

notes.statement: Smith et al. (2020) mined transcriptomic datasets and found that NRROS was enriched more than 50-fold in human microglia compared with whole brain. In mouse brain, Nrros expression was similarly enriched in microglia and was higher in CNS perivascular macrophages than in parenchymal microglia.
quotes: The expression of NRROS was enriched > 50-fold in microglia compared to whole brain, indicating that microglia are the major cell type expressing NRROS in human brain parenchyma.
Comparison of parenchymal microglia with CNS perivascular macrophages (PVMs) showed significantly greater expression in the latter.

notes.statement: Smith et al. (2020) identified homozygous truncating NRROS variants in both families. They noted that p.Gln593* had not been recorded before and that p.Gly420AlafsTer14 was seen on only 1 of 251,438 alleles in gnomAD. No cellular material was available for functional study.
quotes: Cellular material was not available from any of the patients. However, both of these variants are predicted to result in a truncated protein, and both are very rare, with the p.(Gln593*) not previously recorded, and the p.(Gly420AlafsTer14) reported on only 1 of 251,438 alleles on gnomAD.

notes.statement: Smith et al. (2020) reported that all 3 children were born after a normal pregnancy and had unremarkable early development. Refractory seizures and neurodegeneration began in the second year of life, and the children died between 27 and 36 months of age. Imaging first showed fine calcification at the depths of the cerebral gyri with normal white matter. Later imaging showed more calcification, severe atrophy and diffuse white matter signal changes.
quotes: in the second year of life, they experienced the onset of refractory seizures and neurodegeneration, leading to death between the ages of 27 and 36 months.

Neuroimaging initially demonstrated fine calcification at the depths of the cerebral gyri, with normal white matter (Fig. 1). As disease progressed, repeat imaging revealed increased calcification, severe generalized atrophy with ventricular dilatation, and diffuse signal changes in cerebral and cerebellar white matter.

notes.statement: Smith et al. (2020) noted that the patients' features recapitulated those of Nrros-deficient mice. These mice showed progressive neurological decline from 2 to 3 months of age, died by 6 months, and had neuronal loss, demyelination, axonal pathology, astrogliosis and foamy macrophages without immune-mediated inflammation.
quotes: Nrros−/−mice exhibited progressive neurological decline, including motor defects and abnormal locomotor activity, from age 2–3 months and death by 6 months of age.
Of note, there was no indication of immune-mediated inflammation in our case or either of these mouse models.

notes.statement: Wong et al. (2017) found that mice deficient in Nrros, a myeloid-expressed transmembrane protein of the endoplasmic reticulum, developed spontaneous neurological disorders with defects in motor function, and died before 6 months of age. Nrros-/- mice showed astrogliosis and lacked normal CD11b-hi/CD45-lo microglia, without detectable demyelination or neuronal loss; instead, perivascular macrophage-like myeloid cells populated the CNS.
quotes: NRROS-deficient (Nrros-/-) mice show defects in motor functions and die before 6 months of age.

Nrros-/- mice display astrogliosis and lack normal CD11bhiCD45lo microglia, but they show no detectable demyelination or neuronal loss. Instead, perivascular macrophage-like myeloid cells populate the Nrros-/- CNS.

notes.statement: Using Cx3cr1-driven deletion of Nrros in mice, Wong et al. (2017) showed that Nrros has a crucial role in establishing microglia during early embryonic stages. Nrros was required for normal expression of Sall1 and other microglial genes important for microglial development and function.
quotes: Cx3cr1-driven deletion of Nrros shows its crucial role in microglial establishment during early embryonic stages.
NRROS is required for normal expression of Sall1 and other microglial genes that are important for microglial development and function.
